articles.author: Elon Musk
articles.description:
RT Mario Nawfal
MARS CITY "TERMINUS": ELON'S PERFECT SCI-FI TRIBUTE
Elon's suggestion to name Mars' first city "Terminus" gives total sci-fi goosebumps!
This isn't just a random name—it's a heartfelt nod to Asimov's Foundation series, where Terminus stood as humanity's last hope at the edge of the galaxy.
There's something deeply poetic about Mars being our own real-life Terminus—the edge of our current reach and the beginning of something incredible. 
The literary connection feels like a beautiful bridge between the dreams we've had for generations and the future we're actually building.
Elon's democratic sentiment—"it will be up to the people of Mars to decide"—shows he gets that true space colonization means letting Martians (yes, actual future Martians) create their own identity rather than having Earth dictate everything.
This isn't about symbolic flags but creating a thriving second branch of humanity that could persist independently. 
Self-determination means self-sufficiency, with Terminus generating its own resources and eventually its own distinct culture to truly make humanity a multiplanetary species capable of surviving even if Earth faced catastrophe.
Media Source: @tsarnick @elonmusk


Elon Musk: @DimaZeniuk It’s from Asimov’s Foundation. 
But I’m open to other ideas.
Ultimately, it will be up to the people of Mars to decide.
